model_interface.notes: The interface is missing 'preferredLanguage', which is already read and written by src/api/userRouter.ts. This is a live type-safety gap independent of any future changes.

risk_flags: Accepts 'Record<string, any>' instead of 'UserProfile' — no compile-time binding to the model at all.
formatAnalyticsPayload uses Object.entries to iterate all keys dynamically; any new field added to UserProfile is silently consumed without awareness.

Calls value.toString().toLowerCase() on every field unconditionally — non-string fields (booleans, nested objects, arrays, numbers) will not throw at compile time but will produce corrupted or misleading telemetry strings at runtime.

dispatchEvent passes the raw user object directly to formatAnalyticsPayload with no filtering or field allowlist — new optional fields on UserProfile will automatically leak into the telemetry payload.
There is no guard against null or undefined values; a new optional field (value: undefined) will throw 'Cannot read properties of undefined' at runtime when .toString() is called.

Reads and writes 'user.preferredLanguage' on lines 25, 42, 43, 48 — this field is NOT declared on the UserProfile interface, so TypeScript will error unless the file suppresses it (it does, via 'as UserProfile' cast on line 57).

POST /users handler casts 'req.body' as 'Partial<UserProfile> & { id: string }' and then forces the result 'as UserProfile' — this bypasses exhaustive field checking and allows objects with missing required fields to be stored silently.
The Map<string, UserProfile> on line 11 is typed correctly, but the values stored via users.set() are created through unsafe casts, so runtime objects may not match the declared interface.

Comment on line 4-6 acknowledges the model assumption ('preferredLanguage?: string') but this field is not in the actual interface — meaning the file is intentionally operating outside the type contract.
Any new optional field added to UserProfile will NOT be reflected in the PATCH handler logic, meaning it will be ignored silently in updates — no compile-time signal that the handler needs updating.

summary.highest_risk: src/analytics/eventTracker.ts — dynamic Object.entries iteration with unconditional toString() will silently corrupt telemetry for any non-string field added to UserProfile, including optional fields with undefined values which will throw at runtime.
summary.secondary_risk: src/api/userRouter.ts — operates on a field (preferredLanguage) not in the declared interface, uses unsafe 'as UserProfile' casts that defeat TypeScript's structural checks, and will silently ignore new optional fields in PATCH logic.
summary.model_gap: UserProfile interface itself is incomplete — it does not declare 'preferredLanguage' despite active production use of that field in userRouter.ts.
